articles.title: Prahaar: Rajkummar Rao — and a Stunning Kasab — Make the 26/11 Trial Gripping
articles.excerpt: Critics hand the 26/11 trial drama the week's strongest notices — anchored by Rajkummar Rao's restraint and a Kasab performance reviewers call stunning.
articles.image_caption: Rajkummar Rao, who plays prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam in Prahaar.
articles.nri_angle: The 26/11 trial is a story every Indian family followed from abroad; critics call Prahaar the strongest Indian release of the week — a focused Hindi courtroom drama playing now in US and UK cinemas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.rating_consensus: Critics hand Prahaar the week's strongest notices: a restrained, performance-led courtroom drama whose only real fault is length — anchored by Rajkummar Rao and stolen by Lalit Prabhakar's Kasab.

articles.title: Ranabaali: A Sincere Famine Epic That Wins Respect but Tests Patience
articles.excerpt: Reviewers honour the famine subject and the craft — and nearly all of them ask why a film this sincere needed to be this slow.
articles.image_caption: Vijay Deverakonda, who leads the famine epic Ranabaali.
articles.nri_angle: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna's first film together after their wedding, and a rare Telugu epic about the 1870s Great Famine — playing now across the US Telugu circuit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.rating_consensus: Critics respect Ranabaali more than they enjoy it: an honest, beautifully mounted famine drama with committed leads, weighed down by a slow, predictable second half — a film to admire, at a pace you have to accept.

articles.title: Jailer 2: Critics Say Rajinikanth's Swagger Carries a Sequel That Runs Out of Plot
articles.excerpt: Reviewers split the film in two — a rollicking, comedy-rich first half powered by the Superstar, and a second half where the writing stops keeping up with him.
articles.image_caption: 'Jailer 2' directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, now in theaters.
articles.nri_angle: Rajinikanth's biggest worldwide opening ever is playing now in US, UK and Canadian cinemas in Tamil with Telugu and Hindi versions — a genuine big-screen event for the diaspora, even if the film itself splits critics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.rating_consensus: Critics converge on a 3-star verdict: a rollicking first half built on Rajinikanth's swagger, Nelson's dark comedy and Anirudh's score, followed by an overcrowded second half where the writing stops keeping up — good fun, short of the first film.

articles.title: Jailer 2's Telugu Bet: ₹45 Crore Rights, a Slow Start and a Weekend to Save It

articles.image_caption: Producer Naga Vamsi, left, who bought the Telugu rights, and Rajinikanth as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian in Jailer 2. The Telugu version opened slowly despite strong Tamil collections.
articles.nri_angle: North America shows the same pattern as the Telugu states, and the territory's break-even is about $7 million — diaspora turnout this weekend decides both.
